questions.stem:
Which line contains the bug?
```python
status = "ready"
if status = "ready":
    launch()
print("done")
```

Treats a normal assignment as the defect
Blames an unrelated trailing statement

questions.subject: PYTHON
questions.learningObjective: Reason about lists — essentials 01 when reading code.
questions.stem:
Which line is the bug? The loop should walk every index of items.
```python
n = len(items)
for i in range(1, n):
    print(i)
print("done")
```

options.misconception: Points at the body, which merely prints the index it is given
Blames the length lookup, which is correct
Blames an unrelated trailing statement

questions.explanation: range(1, n) starts at 1, so index 0 is never visited even though the loop is meant to walk every index; range(n) starts at 0 and stops before n, covering them all. Option A is wrong because print only displays the index supplied by the loop. Option C is wrong because len(items) is the correct upper bound. Option D is wrong because it is a separate statement after the loop.
questions.hint: Follow the lines as written and find the one whose behaviour departs from the intended task.
